title: Proper base change over a finite extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $I=(\varpi)$, using [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes $X,Y,X',Y'$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Assume $f$ and $f'$ are proper and that the geometric fibers of $f$ have dimension at most some $e\geq0$, as in [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete]. Use the raw rational categories $\Dbc(T,E)=\Dbc(T_{\Proet},A)[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Denote by $Rf_*,Rf'_*,Lg^*,Lg'^*$ the rational extensions, as in [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], of the integral direct images and completed pullbacks in that corollary. The specified rational exchange is the extension of its completed integral exchange. For every $K\in\Dbc(X,E)$ its component is an isomorphism
$$
 Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*Lg'^*K
 \quad\text{in }\Dbc(Y',E).
$$

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], rationalization has the same objects as the integral category. Regard $K$ as its integral object $K_0\in\Dbc(X_{\Proet},A)$; this is part of the category definition, not a lattice-existence theorem. Apply [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete] to $K_0$. All four schemes are noetherian and finite-dimensional, both vertical maps are proper, and the fiber bound is supplied. Its annihilator condition holds with $N=\ell$: by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=(\varpi)=I$ and $\ell$ annihilates $A/I$; it is invertible on all four schemes. We obtain the specified integral natural isomorphism $\eta$ between the two composite functors, with both endpoints in the integral category on $Y'$.

source.place: ## Proof; explicit rationalization of the integral exchange

proof.text:
First check the individual functor hypotheses of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport], not only its composites. Apply [cor-weil-pbc-constructible-complete] to the cartesian square with both vertical arrows $f$ and horizontal identities of $X,Y$. It applies to every integral constructible object on $X$, with the stated fiber bound $e$, and its displayed composites give preservation by $Rf_*$. Apply it likewise with both vertical arrows $f'$ and horizontal identities of $X',Y'$ to obtain preservation by $Rf'_*$. The fiber bound for $f'$ is $e$: for a geometric point $y':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y'$, the given cartesian identification gives $X'\times_{Y'}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\cong X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ with structure map $g y'$, so these geometric fibers are isomorphic. For either horizontal morphism $h=g$ or $h=g'$, apply the corollary to the cartesian square with vertical identities on the source and target of $h$ and both horizontal arrows $h$, with fiber bound zero. This gives preservation by $Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ on every integral constructible object on its source. All these squares have noetherian finite-dimensional corners, proper vertical maps and the same invertible annihilator $N=\ell$ as in step 1. Identity direct image is the identity because termwise direct image for the identity map does nothing to a K-injective representative. Completed identity pullback is the identity on complete objects: by [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] it is ordinary identity pullback followed by derived completion, whose completion unit is an isomorphism on complete objects. Thus the four restrictions are defined without assuming a uniform cohomological reduction interval from the termwise local-model bounds. The left derived constructions preserve shifts and cones on their resolving complexes; the right derived direct image does so on K-injective representatives, since shifts and cones of K-injectives remain K-injective by the Hom characterization of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Termwise additive operations commute with the two finite summands and differential in a cone. Together with [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality], these constructions give triangulated functors on the full constructible subcategories.

Use [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] on the integral functors and exchange of step 1. Here scalar linearity can be checked directly in the constructions of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]: inverse image and tensor send multiplication by $a\in A$ to multiplication by the same constant $a$, and a compatible family in an inverse limit is multiplied componentwise. Ordinary module direct image has the same property on sections. For the left derived constructions, represent a map by a roof $C\xleftarrow{s}P\xrightarrow{u}D$ in the resolving class used to compute the operation. Multiplying the map by $a$ replaces $u$ by $au$, leaving $s$ fixed. The termwise operation sends this to $F(au)=aF(u)$, so the derived roof $F(u)F(s)^{-1}$ is also multiplied by $a$. For the right derived constructions (direct image and inverse limit), fix K-injective representatives $C\to I_C,D\to I_D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], a derived morphism has a unique homotopy-class representative $h:I_C\to I_D$. The representative for $ah$ is its scalar multiple: localization is $A$-linear, so injectivity of that Hom bijection proves this equality without requiring a scalar-linear resolution-choice functor. Applying ordinary direct image or inverse limit termwise sends $ah$ to $aF(h)$. Both also preserve homotopies, since applying the additive termwise operation to $h_1-h_2=dt+td$ gives the same equation. Addition is preserved by these same formulas. Thus the integral operations are $A$-linear, and restrictions to the full constructible subcategories preserve these equalities. The corollary supplies their triangulated composites on those categories. Rational transport gives the extended exchange with component $\eta_{K_0}\otimes1$. The extension of each composite agrees with the composite of the extensions: on a pure morphism $u\otimes b$ both send it to $F(G(u))\otimes b$, and these pure tensors generate each Hom module. Uniqueness in rational transport then identifies the specified rational exchange with this extension.

source.place: ## Proof; explicit rationalization of the integral exchange

proof.text:
Let $v=\eta_{K_0}^{-1}$ in the integral category on $Y'$. Composition and identities in [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] give
$$(v\otimes1)\circ(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)=(v\circ\eta_{K_0})\otimes1=\mathrm{id}\otimes1,$$
and likewise $(\eta_{K_0}\otimes1)\circ(v\otimes1)=\mathrm{id}\otimes1$. Thus $v\otimes1$ is the inverse of the specified rational exchange. Every rational object is covered by step 1, so this proves the assertion for all $K$, including zero and objects killed by a power of $\varpi$.
